title: Private key-wrap timeout causing intermittent role-binding misapply and SSO audit gaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:

Several enterprise Private customers observed missing or delayed audit events and transient role-binding misapplications during a high-load maintenance window on 2026-03-12. Symptoms included: SSO logins that completed but had no corresponding audit entry for the role-binding step, and short-lived elevation where a role binding applied to a session for 1-3 seconds and then reverted. This caused two customer escalations (one high-security tenant) and triggered an on-call paging event.

Root cause hypothesis (validated by traces):
- The key-wrap operation against customer-managed KMS occasionally hit a 3s network timeout threshold under bursty traffic patterns.
- When key-wrap times out, our ephem-key initialisation code attempted a synchronous fallback path that raced with the RBAC write path. The fallback path used a cached ORB token which is scoped differently, causing a temporary binding using a broader role set.
- Audit emitter is hooked to the successful completion path of the key-wrap; timeouts produced a code path where audit events were skipped or emitted after the role write was already reverted.
- The combination of race + delayed audit led to: (a) missing audit record at time of elevation, (b) short-lived incorrect role state visible to the customer, (c) noisy reconciliation jobs later correcting state which produced further audit noise.

Reproduction steps (dev env):
1) Deploy a private control-plane with KMS proxy configured and inject artificial 3000-3500ms latencies on WrapKey RPC.
2) Simulate parallel SSO assertions (50tps) for a single tenant and trigger a role binding that requires KMS unwrap/rewrap.
3) Observe that 2-4% of requests follow the fallback path and that role binding applies briefly then reverts; audit emitter misses events.

Immediate mitigations applied (Mar 12-13):
- Increased WrapKey RPC client timeout to 8s for customer-managed KMS in Private clusters to reduce transient fallback activation. (config change rolled to affected clusters)
- Disabled the synchronous cached ORB fallback path by feature flag to prevent scope-downgrade race; flag: feature.disable_orb_fallback=true.
- Enabled additional audit buffering to force durable write-through for pending events until either timeout or explicit failure path.
These mitigations reduced visible incidents by ~90% in canary clusters.

Permanent fix plan (this ticket):
1) Replace synchronous fallback with an async compensating workflow: if WrapKey times out, enqueue a compensating reconciliation job that will reapply correct-scoped role-bindings only after validated key-wrap completion.
2) Guarantee audit path always emits a pre-write "intent-to-bind" event (PERSISTENT) before RBAC write; on reconciliation emit finalization event. This avoids missing audit-of-intent.
3) Harden KMS client: implement adaptive backoff + circuit-breaker and add metrics for Wrap/Unwrap p95/p99.
4) Add deterministic unit and integration tests that simulate KMS latency and validate no temporary role escalation can surface to callers.
5) Add a chaos-test to private-cluster nightly suite that injects KMS latencies and asserts audit completeness.

Implementation notes:
- Code changes are in runtime/kms/wrap_manager.go and rbac/role_writer.go. The PR reference is in links above.
- New DB table audit_intents(created_at, request_id, tenant_id, action) will be appended to the existing audit store. We will migrate with a lightweight backfill for last 30d.
- Rollout will use canary percentage-based rollout via Console: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for wrap_manager: simulate timeouts and verify enqueue of reconciliation job.
- Integration tests with a KMS mock that returns delayed WrapKey responses.
- E2E on a private dev cluster with real KMS proxy and SSO flow validation.
- Add alert: if any canary cluster shows >0.5% transient role-binding mismatches during rollout pause, abort.

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR to main after 2 approvals and security sign-off (required).
- Deploy to staging, run integration/chaos suite for 4 hours.
- Canary rollout to 3 private customers (manual selection with high-security tenant excluded until 25% step).
- Observe for 6 hours with telemetry dashboards (WrapKey latency, audit_intent count, reconciliation job lag, RBAC write rate).
- Proceed to 25% -> 100% if stable.

Postmortem and customer communication:
- Prepare a short incident summary for impacted tenants explaining root cause and mitigation steps (owner: PM).
- Draft postmortem doc and RCA (assigned to creator).
- Offer follow-up remediation support and additional audit dump export for impacted tenants on request.

Open questions & decisions to make:
- Migration window for audit_intents backfill (online vs maintenance window).
- Whether ORB cached token fallback should be entirely removed or reworked with stricter scoping.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Marco Liu: implement async compensating workflow and update role_writer to emit audit intents. (in progress)
- Ravi Desai (SRE): prepare canary mesh config and monitoring dashboards.
- Sofia Martinez (Security): run security review and sign-off on new audit_intent schema.
- Priya Nair (PM): draft customer-facing incident summary and coordinate notifications.

Expected completion: targeted ship on 2026-03-18, contingent on security review and canary stability.
